rows.note: The description says any values, so four unbounded one-to-three digit groups separated by dots is the rule it asks for.

The description says a single number is a list of one, and the recorded rule \d+,\d+ requires a comma, so it never matches '1' at all; the row's own must_reject of '1' writes the mistake down instead of catching it.

The description says the path begins with a drive letter and a colon and stops there, while the recorded rule also demands a following backslash; C: satisfies the sentence and not the rule, and nothing here says which the desk meant.
The rule keys on the literal token, allows whitespace around the colon, and puts the value in the one capturing group, which is what capturing only the value means.
The scheme group is optional and ends in ://, the host class matches a dotted name, and the one-or-more quantifier is why the empty string is rejected.
